title: Two carts stick: how fast now?
hook: A cart slams into a parked one and they lock together. Does the pair keep the speed?

knows: a moving thing hitting a still thing slows down
mass as how heavy something is
doesNotKnow: that total momentum is conserved when nothing outside pushes

misconception: After two carts stick, the pair keeps the first cart's speed, or the speeds simply average.
objective: The learner can explain that the total mass x speed is the same before and after the carts stick, so a heavier pair moves more slowly: 2 kg x 3 m/s shared by 3 kg gives 2 m/s.

claims.text: When nothing outside pushes along the track, the total momentum (mass x velocity) of the two carts is the same before and after they collide.
claims.source: Conservation of linear momentum for an isolated system (Newton's third law). Halliday, Resnick and Walker, Fundamentals of Physics, ch. 9.

claims.text: A 2 kg cart at 3 m/s that sticks to a stationary 1 kg cart leaves at 2 m/s: 6 kg m/s shared by 3 kg.
Motion (kinetic) energy is not conserved when the carts stick: 9 J before, 6 J after with the 1 kg cart; the rest goes into deformation and heat.
claims.source: 1/2 x 2 x 3^2 = 9 J; 1/2 x 3 x 2^2 = 6 J. Perfectly inelastic collision (Halliday, Resnick and Walker, ch. 9.6).

claims.text: The lesson assumes a frictionless track and carts that stick perfectly.
claims.source: Stated idealisation on the stage ('Frictionless. Carts stick.'). With friction the pair would slow after the crash; momentum is still conserved during the brief collision itself (impulse approximation).

recall.question: A 1,000 kg car at 10 m/s rear-ends a stopped 1,000 kg car and they lock bumpers. Ignoring friction, how fast do they move together?
recall.why: Momentum is conserved: 1,000 x 10 = 2,000 x v, so v = 5 m/s. Twice the mass shares the same momentum at half the speed.
